claims.text: The AWSx ELB component integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC to give compute running in AWS configurable network accessibility.

Targeting an EC2 instance with a load balancer requires opening egress from the instance to the load balancer for health checks, ensuring the LB security group has the ingress rule, creating instances in the same VPC, and attaching the target group.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
The Pulumi AWS registry has API docs for the LaunchTemplate resource at /registry/packages/aws/api-docs/ec2/launchtemplate/.
In AWSx, passing the load balancer's target group in an ECS task definition's `portMappings` causes AWSx to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw aws.ecs requires manual security group management.
The awsx-load-balanced-fargate-nginx example exports a stack output named `url`.
ALBs offer two features that make them more attractive for ECS: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
Pulumi recommends ALBs for ECS services unless a service requires a feature only available with NLBs.
By default, an AWSx load balancer is created internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
AWSx load balancers accept either a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs) for an explicit subnet list.
NLB listeners support protocols TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC while ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP.
AWS docs page rule-action-types.html contains #fixed-response-actions and #redirect-actions anchors.
AWS documentation has a listener rules page at listener-rules.html.
The `deregistrationDelay` range is 0–3600 seconds with a default of 300.
The `slowStart` range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable, disabled by default.
Target group `targetType` possible values are instance, ip, lambda, and alb; default is instance; IPs must be in VPC private range, RFC 1918, or RFC 6598 (100.64.0.0/10).
Health check `interval` range is 5–300 seconds with default 30 seconds.
Health check `healthyThreshold` range is 2–10 with default 3.
Health check `unhealthyThreshold` range is 2–10, default 3, and for NLBs must equal healthyThreshold.
Health check `timeout` range is 2–120 seconds; AWS defaults are 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
